absent: Full layouts of PMU, vCPU, VM arch, hypercall config, shared-info, and async-fault structures.
Ownership and locking for PMU bitmaps and counter fields beyond the shown atomic clear and async-writer note.
Contracts of unrouted helpers for enable checks, allow-listing, masking, fixed-field extraction, and host perf interaction.
Backend hooks for PMU cleanup, TSC offset propagation, nested scaling queries, hypercall patching, and guest memory writes.
TSC scaling arithmetic, clocksource selection, and tracing payloads.
Xen feature enablement, blob provisioning, guest-mode detection, and page-cache refresh semantics.
Async page-fault hash, probe-sequence, slot-count, token allocation, and arch dequeue and ready hooks.
Caller-visible error codes for hypercall-page failures and PAT failure handling.

findings.text: PMU refresh exposes handling and cleanup operations that process pending reprogramming work, release idle host resources, and refresh emulation state for affected counters.

Event handling snapshots the pending reprogramming set into a local bitmap sized by the maximum counter index and clears only those snapshotted bits from shared state through an atomic clear, tolerating asynchronous writers outside the vCPU mutex. Counters whose reprogramming fails have their pending bit set again for a later refresh without issuing a new request.

Counter reprogramming takes a mediated path that only refreshes an event filter when mediation is active. Otherwise it pauses the counter to learn whether an emulated overflow occurred, returns early when global enable, local enable, or allow-list checks fail, and synthesizes an overflow indication outside PMI context when pausing detected a wrap. A pin-control request is ignored with a one-time notice.

For fixed counters the selection value is translated from the fixed control field by mapping kernel, user, and PMI enable subfields onto corresponding selection attributes, and the stored configuration becomes the fixed control slice rather than the selection value. If stored configuration is unchanged and the existing host event can be resumed, reprogramming reuses it; otherwise it releases the old event, updates stored configuration, and creates a new raw host event shaped by privilege and interrupt attributes.

Overflow handling distinguishes precise host events from ordinary counters. Precise events outside PMI context suppress guest notification, while precise events inside PMI context set a shared buffer-overflow status bit only once. Ordinary counters set a per-index bit in global status. A PMI request is raised against the owning vCPU only when interrupt signaling is armed and notification was not suppressed.

Host event creation uses a pinned, idle-excluded, host-excluded raw event whose user and kernel exclusion and interrupt behavior derive from selection attributes and whose period derives from the current counter value. A checkpointed-transactional attribute combined with host transactional-memory support forces a zero period to keep allocation from failing. When the index is marked for precise sampling, a calibrated precision level is attached.

The sampling period is the negated counter value masked to the counter width, with a zero result replaced by one plus the mask so every counter has a positive period. The precise level is elevated for two model-specific counter and CPU combinations and is otherwise a minimal nonzero level that marks the host event as precise for PMI routing.

Pausing accumulates host progress into the software counter when an unpaused host event exists, snapshots the masked value after accumulation, folds in emulated progress, clears emulated progress, marks the counter paused, and reports whether the final masked value wrapped below the snapshot. Resuming refuses when no host event exists, when a sampling event rejects the recalibrated period, or when precise-mode state disagrees with the precise-enable bit.

Mediated refresh computes eligibility as locally enabled and allow-listed. General-purpose counters update only the enable bit of a shadow selection value, while fixed counters update only the nibble belonging to the counter index inside a shadow fixed-control value, setting shadow bits from guest values when eligible and clearing them otherwise.

The PMU container maps back to its owning vCPU through the architecture-specific PMU member. Global enable is vacuously true on hardware without a global control register and otherwise reflects the per-index bit in global control.

Cleanup clears the deferred-cleanup flag, computes valid-but-unused counter indexes by subtracting the in-use set from the valid set, stops host events for counters in that set that are not locally enabled, invokes a backend-specific cleanup hook, and then clears the in-use set.

TSC management exposes operations to compute a level-one offset for a target value, synchronize a vCPU clock under the TSC write lock, write a level-one offset with nested handling, and combine level-one and level-two offsets with scaling.

Level-one offset computation scales the current host timestamp by the vCPU scaling ratio and subtracts it from the desired guest value. Nested offset combination passes the level-one offset through unchanged when the level-two multiplier equals the default ratio and otherwise scales it by the fractional-bit shift before adding the level-two offset. A small helper adds a signed adjustment to the stored level-one offset through the write path.

Synchronization under the write lock records a base time and elapsed interval, treats a zero target or an explicit zero write as forced synchronization, and treats a user write within a one-second virtual-time window of the prior write as intended synchronization only when a prior user write exists. On stable clocks a matched synchronization reuses the current generation offset, while on unstable clocks it advances the target by elapsed cycles and recomputes before stamping generation bookkeeping.
All TSC synchronization and generation bookkeeping is serialized by the VM-wide TSC write lock taken with interrupts saved; the inner synchronization helper requires that lock to be held.

Master-clock use requires every online vCPU to share the current generation plus a host clocksource backed by TSC; a master-clock update request is issued when the desired state toggles or when a new generation starts while master-clock use is active. The unstable check treats Hyper-V clock mode as stable and otherwise defers to the generic instability test.

Writing a TSC offset is a no-op when the guest clock is protected. Otherwise it records the new level-one offset, and in guest mode combines it with level-two offset and multiplier state through backend hooks to form the effective offset, while outside guest mode the effective offset equals the level-one value; a backend hook then propagates the result.
Page-attribute-table validation rejects any value with reserved bits set in any byte and accepts only per-byte type encodings drawn from the architecturally valid set.

Xen hypercall-page handling has a full implementation that manages mode tracking and guest page contents and a fallback inline definition that unconditionally reports failure, selected by build configuration.

Hypercall-page writes split the input into a page number and page address, update cached guest-mode state under the Xen lock and reinitialize shared info on a mode change, then either synthesize a trap-based page or copy a user-provided page. Synthesized mode only accepts page zero and fills the page with repeated fixed-size slots each carrying the slot index as immediate plus trap and return behavior with padding. Provided-blob mode bounds-checks the page number against a mode-specific size and copies one page from the mode-specific user address.

Shared-info initialization refreshes the page cache until it validates for a full page, fetches the wall-clock epoch, selects long or compatibility layouts based on mode, and publishes seconds, sub-second, and high-seconds fields under an odd-even version sequence with ordering barriers so readers observe a consistent snapshot.
Compatibility wall-clock base is at byte offset 2304 with high seconds at 2340; 64-bit wall-clock base is at 3072 with high seconds at 3100; time-info version is at offset zero.

Hypercall-page MSR identification has an enabled variant that returns true only for a nonzero MSR equal to the configured hypercall MSR when the Xen feature is enabled, and a disabled variant that always reports false.

Asynchronous page-fault completion drains the per-vCPU done queue while entries remain and the architecture allows dequeuing, removing each entry under the per-vCPU async lock, invoking architecture ready hooks, unlinking queue membership, decrementing the queued count, and flushing and freeing the work item.

Present delivery distinguishes broadcast wakeups, which use an all-ones token, from targeted completions, which remove the faulting frame from the per-vCPU set. When a wakeup or injected-not-present completion has paravirtual async support and the token can be delivered to the guest, a ready flag is published and a fixed LAPIC interrupt with the configured vector is sent. The halted mark is cleared and the vCPU is moved to runnable state.

Removal of a faulting frame from the fixed probe table locates the expected slot by hash, warns and returns on mismatch, and otherwise clears the slot and compacts forward entries by backward shifting while preserving cyclic probe-order invariants until an empty slot is reached.

Reprogramming state can be mutated asynchronously outside the vCPU mutex, so only snapshotted bits may be cleared. Failed reprogramming must not issue a new request or the guest can stall. Precise host events suppress synthetic overflow notifications outside PMI context to avoid spurious buffer-overflow signaling.

TSC writes are ignored when the guest clock is protected, and legacy user writes carry a one-second matching tolerance that can misclassify a genuinely short-lived restored guest as synchronized. Hypercall-page synthesis assumes a fixed slot size dividing the page and treats nonzero pages or out-of-range blob indexes as failures; shared-info publication relies on version sequencing and barriers for reader consistency.

Xen mode state is protected by the Xen mutex, shared-info cache access combines source-read protection with an interrupt-saving read lock and a refresh-until-valid loop, and async completion queue mutation is protected by the per-vCPU async spin lock.
Deleting a faulting frame that does not match the probed slot indicates table inconsistency and is reported once without mutating the table.
